Probably never happened. Almost certainly never happened. And even if it did, it's probably misinterpreted.

The French revolution was catalyzed by a (somewhat manufactured) shortage of bread flour. Due to simple supply and demand, the price of bread rose with the cost of flour. Parisians pretty much lived off bread, and even a small change the price was worse than a spike in gasoline prices in modern America. But there was also brioche, a heavy eggy cake-like bread made from cake flour. It was more profitable than bread for bakers, so there were controls on its price (basically it was indexed to the price of bread so bakers couldn't play like they were out of bread but force a sale of brioche at a greater cost and profit). IF Marie Antoinette said that, what she was implying (though poorly worded, at least without context) that the price controls should be altered so the starving people could get brioche where it is available.
